outline.description: This chapter sets the stage for the textbook by introducing the intersection of Large Language Models (LLMs) and tabular data analysis. It defines the core problem of few-shot learning in tabular domains and highlights the limitations of current approaches, motivating the need for a feature-engineering perspective.
subtopics: The rise of Large Language Models and their reasoning capabilities.
The importance of tabular data in real-world machine learning applications.
Challenges in few-shot learning: data scarcity and spurious correlations.
Current limitations of LLM-based tabular learning: inference costs, prompt size limits, and training constraints.
The paradigm shift: treating LLMs as feature engineers rather than end-to-end predictors.
Overview of FeatLLM objectives: efficiency, interpretability, and performance.

outline.chapter_title: Foundations: Few-Shot Learning and Language-Interfaced Models
outline.description: This chapter provides the necessary background knowledge required to understand the FeatLLM framework. It reviews existing literature on few-shot learning for tabular data and explores previous attempts to interface tabular data with language models.
subtopics: Overview of few-shot learning strategies (semi-supervised learning, data augmentation, pre-training).
Language-interfaced tabular learning: serializing data into text prompts.
In-context learning vs. parameter-efficient fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA, IA3).
Introduction to key baselines: TabLLM, TabPFN, STUNT, and TransTab.
The concept of prior knowledge in LLMs and its potential application in domain-specific tasks.

outline.chapter_title: The FeatLLM Methodology: An Architectural Overview
outline.description: This chapter presents the high-level architecture of the FeatLLM framework. It describes the end-to-end pipeline from input data to final prediction, explaining how the framework separates feature generation from prediction.
subtopics: Problem formulation: defining datasets, feature names, and labels for k-shot learning.
The core philosophy: extracting 'rules' (criteria) instead of direct predictions.
Pipeline overview: Prompting -> Rule Extraction -> Parsing -> Feature Generation -> Model Training.
Advantages of decoupling feature engineering from the inference model.
Visualizing the workflow: mapping the journey from raw tabular samples to binary features.

outline.chapter_title: Engineering the Prompt: Extracting Knowledge from LLMs
outline.description: This chapter offers a deep dive into the prompt design strategies employed by FeatLLM. It explains how to structure prompts to guide the LLM through a logical reasoning process to generate high-quality rules.
subtopics: Component 1: Basic Information Description (task, features, and serialized examples).
Data serialization techniques: converting tabular rows into natural language.
Component 2: Reasoning Instructions and the two-step inference process.
Step 1: Inferring causal relationships using prior knowledge without examples.
Step 2: Deduce decisive rules using few-shot demonstrations.
Component 3: Response Instructions for structured and parsable outputs.
Mitigating spurious correlations through structured reasoning.

outline.chapter_title: From Natural Language to Binary Features: Rule Parsing and Application
outline.description: This chapter focuses on the technical implementation of converting LLM-generated text rules into executable code and binary features. It addresses the challenges of parsing natural language and the model used for final classification.
subtopics: The challenge of parsing noisy LLM outputs (syntactic variations).
Leveraging the LLM to write its own parsing code: code generation via semantic understanding.
Feature generation: transforming samples into binary vectors based on rule satisfaction.
Inferring class likelihood: a linear model approach.
Mathematical formulation of the linear model: logits, positive weight projection, and Softmax.
Training the downstream model: optimizing weights to learn rule importance.

outline.chapter_title: Optimization and Robustness: Ensembling with Bagging
outline.description: This chapter explains how FeatLLM ensures robustness and handles large datasets through ensemble methods. It details the bagging techniques used to overcome prompt length limitations and improve prediction stability.
subtopics: The necessity of ensembling in few-shot regimes.
Introducing randomness: temperature settings and example ordering.
Bagging strategies: sub-sampling features and instances.
Overcoming prompt size limitations: handling datasets with large numbers of attributes.
Ensemble prediction: averaging probabilities across multiple trials.
The concept of self-consistency in LLM reasoning.

outline.chapter_title: Empirical Evaluation: Datasets, Baselines, and Results
outline.description: This chapter presents the experimental setup and results, demonstrating the efficacy of FeatLLM across various domains. It compares the framework against traditional machine learning and contemporary LLM-based methods.
subtopics: Benchmark datasets: standard UCI datasets vs. new/synthetic datasets (e.g., Cultivars, Sequence-type).
Experimental setup: k-shot learning parameters and evaluation metrics (AUC).
Baselines: Traditional ML (LogReg, XGBoost), pre-trained models (TabPFN), and LLM methods (TabLLM).
Performance analysis: FeatLLM vs. baselines in low-data regimes.
Data efficiency: achieving competitive performance with significantly fewer shots.

outline.chapter_title: Deep Dive: Analytical Insights and Robustness Checks
outline.description: This chapter goes beyond performance metrics to analyze *why* FeatLLM works. It covers ablation studies, runtime analysis, and the quality of the generated features.
subtopics: Ablation studies: the impact of tuning, ensembling, descriptions, and reasoning steps.
Training and inference time comparison: FeatLLM vs. expensive LLM query methods.
Quality analysis of generated rules: measuring informativeness before and after weight tuning.
Robustness to spurious correlations: handling irrelevant columns.
Hyper-parameter analysis: the effect of the number of rules and ensemble size.

outline.description: The final chapter summarizes the key contributions of FeatLLM and discusses its broader implications. It also addresses limitations and outlines potential future research directions.
subtopics: Summary of contributions: bridging LLMs and tabular learning via feature engineering.
Broader impact: applications in finance, healthcare, and other domains with high labeling costs.
Potential risks: societal biases in LLM prior knowledge and misinformation.
Limitations: focus on low-shot regimes and specific feature types.
Future directions: expanding to larger datasets, enhancing interpretability, and exploring diverse feature types.
